title: A group adds leak shapes as data and may replace the leak scan as extension point leak_scan, and every replaced guard is named by kbext.py guards and kbmon --status
goal: the leak.shapes of the settings layers, each a kind and a regular expression, join the shapes kbcommon.leak_hits refuses; a shape that does not compile or matches the empty string is refused when the layers load, naming the layer; extensions.leak_scan names a function with kbpublic.file_hits' signature that replaces it in this clone; kbext.py guards --root WS prints each replaced guard with its module and layer, or one line saying the shipped guards run; kbmon.py --status all names a replaced guard in its first lines; git.md and extending.md say which paths still run the shipped guards as this story's gate answers; _tools/test_leaks.py holds one planted failure for a group's added leak shape

gates.question: When a group replaces the leak scan, do kbgit.py contribute and the shared repository's own gate still run the shipped leak scan and guards on what the group gives back?
gates.reason: a group's trust covers its own repository, not what it hands to everyone else; the shared gate never loads a group's extenders

gates.question: When a group's leak.shapes holds a shape that cannot be used (does not compile, matches the empty string, has a kind that is a shipped kind or private-..., or is not an object of exactly kind and pattern), what does a scan that reads the shapes do?
options: refuse with kbext.ExtensionError, naming the layer
skip the shape and scan with the rest
gates.recommendation: refuse with kbext.ExtensionError, naming the layer
gates.reason: a guard never runs on shapes it cannot trust
gates.answer: refuse with kbext.ExtensionError, naming the layer

gates.question: Which paths run the shipped leak scan even where a group replaced it with extension point leak_scan, beyond the contribute path the gate names?
gates.reason: both hand content to everyone else, and publish's verdict cache is keyed apart from a replacing scan's

gates.question: Where does kbmon --status all take its guard lines, and which settings layers do leak.shapes read in a scan?
options: kbmon.py status adds the lines after needs you from kbext.replaced_guards, and the group, clone and user layers are read
mon_status.answer adds the lines, and a kb root layer is read too
gates.recommendation: kbmon.py status adds the lines after needs you from kbext.replaced_guards, and the group, clone and user layers are read
gates.reason: mon_status.answer stays a function of the snapshot, and a scan names no kb root
